output.review_comment:
The changes mix two different pricing models (graduated pricing for bounded tiers, volume pricing for open-ended tier) without explanation. The special case for open-ended tiers appears to be test-specific logic rather than a coherent general algorithm.

Required before approval:
1. Add a PR description explaining what the changes fix and why
2. Justify the special case for open-ended tiers—why use volume pricing (all units at one rate) here when the function is called "graduated_price_cents"?
3. Clarify tier boundary semantics (inclusive/exclusive, 0-indexed/1-indexed) and justify the +1 change
4. Confirm test results show the failing tests now pass
5. Explain why the loop's conditional `if last is None` and the special case logic are both needed if they can both handle open-ended tiers

The special case using `quantity * last_tier[2]` looks like it was added specifically to pass a particular test case rather than being part of a consistent algorithm design.
